'''Edmund Hlawka''' (5 November 1916, [[Bruck an der Mur]], [[Styria]] – 19 February 2009) was an [[Austria]]n [[mathematician]]. He was a leading [[number theorist]]. Hlawka did most of his work at the [[Vienna University of Technology]]. He was also a visiting professor at [[Princeton University]] and the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]]. Hlawka died on 19 February 2009 in [[Vienna]].<ref>[http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2009/02/27/europe/EU-Austria-Obit-Hlawka.php Acclaimed Austrian mathematician Hlawka dies at 92]</ref><ref>[http://www.dieuniversitaet-online.at/personalia/beitrag/news/in-memoriam-edmund-hlawka-1916-2009/297.html In memoriam Edmund Hlawka (1916–2009) (in German)]</ref>

== Education and career ==
Hlawka studied at the [[University of Vienna]] from 1934 to 1938, when he gained his doctorate under [[Nikolaus Hofreiter]]. Among his PhD students were [[Rainer Burkard]], later to become president of the Austrian Society for Operations Research, graph theorist [[Gert Sabidussi]], [[Cole Prize]] winner [[Wolfgang M. Schmidt]], [[Walter Knödel]] who became one of the first German [[computer science]] professors, and [[Hermann Maurer]], also a computer scientist. Through these and other students, Hlawka has over 3000 [[academic genealogy|academic descendants]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=26941}}</ref> Hlawka was awarded the [[Decoration for Services to the Republic of Austria]] in 2007.

* [[Austrian Decoration for Science and Art|Decoration for Science and Art]] (Austria, 1963)<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.parlament.gv.at/PAKT/VHG/XXIV/AB/AB_10542/imfname_251156.pdf | title = Reply to a parliamentary question | language = German | page=147 |trans-title=| access-date = 16 November 2012 }}</ref>
* City of Vienna Prize for the Humanities (1969)
* [[Decoration for Services to the Republic of Austria]], Grand Decoration of Honour in Gold with Star (2007);<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.parlament.gv.at/PAKT/VHG/XXIV/AB/AB_10542/imfname_251156.pdf | title = Reply to a parliamentary question | language = German | page=1779 |trans-title=| access-date = 16 November 2012 }}</ref> Grand Decoration of Honour in Gold (1987)<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.parlament.gv.at/PAKT/VHG/XXIV/AB/AB_10542/imfname_251156.pdf | title = Reply to a parliamentary question | language = German | page=804 |trans-title=| access-date = 16 November 2012 }}</ref>
* [[Wilhelm Exner Medal]] (1982).<ref>Editor, ÖGV. (2015). Wilhelm Exner Medal. Austrian Trade Association. ÖGV. Austria.</ref>
* Joseph Johann Ritter von Prechtl Medal (1989)
* [[Erwin Schrödinger Prize]]
